battle-royale.name: Battle royale
battle-royale.long: Everyone gets the same calculation. A wrong answer or running out of time eliminates you. Time gets shorter every round. The last one standing wins; if every survivor misses the same round, nobody is out.
battle-royale.solo: Chain correct answers for as long as you can. Time gets shorter every round.

speed-race.name: Speed race
speed-race.long: For each calculation, the first correct answer scores the point. One answer per calculation: if you’re wrong, the round goes to the others. On a tie, the fastest overall wins.
speed-race.solo: A series of calculations, one point per correct answer. Your average time tracks your progress.

standard.name: Mental math
standard.long: A calculation appears, you type its result. From “7 + 4” to “125 × 8 − 36 ÷ 4” depending on the level.

right-count.name: Right on target
right-count.long: Some tiles and a target: combine the tiles, each at most once (not necessarily all of them), to hit the target exactly. Each step you add becomes a new tile. There is always a solution; with several players, if nobody finds it, the closest scores when time runs out.

missing.name: Missing number
missing.long: The result is given, but a number or an operator is missing from the calculation: “23 + ? = 41”, “12 ? 4 = 3”. Find what’s missing.

bomb.name: The bomb
bomb.short: Rig a calculation, defuse someone else’s.
bomb.long: Everyone gets the same tiles and builds a calculation: their bomb. Once everyone is ready, each bomb goes to another player, who must find its result. One mistake and you’re out; if your bomb blows someone up, you score a point. Online, two players or more.

gamesPage.title: Games and modes
gamesPage.intro: Pick a game (what you solve), then a mode (how you win). Every game also combines a difficulty level and the operations picked by the lobby’s host.
gamesPage.turnTitle: All at once or taking turns
gamesPage.turnText: All at once: everyone sees the same calculation at the same time. Taking turns: one player answers while the others watch the answer being typed live. Only battle royale eliminates players.

sections.title: Who is responsible for your data?
body: The data controller is the site’s publisher, {publisher}. For any question about your data: {contact}.

sections.title: The data we collect
body: Your account: username, email address, password (stored hashed, never in plain text), sign-up date, profile photo if you add one, and preferences for input (keyboard or voice), division display and end-of-game tips.
Your games: settings, questions asked, answers, response times, scores, rank, Elo and statistics.
Your achievements: achievements and titles earned and progress counters, derived from your games, friends and guild.
Your friends: requests sent and received, friendships, game invitations.
Your guild: the guild you belong to, your role (leader or member), when you joined, invitations, crest, and the time of your last visit to the site (to show members whether you are online).
Your feedback: the message sent from “Send feedback”, its type, the page it came from and, if you are not signed in, the email you choose to leave.
Technical data: the IP address and browser linked to each sign-in, and your IP address to limit repeated attempts (abuse protection).

Anti-cheating: in the daily challenge, your response times are analysed automatically. Times impossible for a human suspend the account from online play (daily challenge, lobbies, dungeons); a doubtful run is only reported to the site’s team. The report keeps the calculations, your answers and their times for as long as your account exists. You can contest a suspension through “Send feedback”: a person then reviews your case.

Without an account, you play as a guest: nothing is saved in solo games, except the daily calc, whose attempt (answers and times, no name) is kept for two days at most so you can save it to an account. Online, your guest name is saved with the game if other players have an account.
Theme, sound and some settings are kept in your browser (local storage) and are never sent to us.

sections.title: Why, and on what legal basis
body: Running the service (account, games, statistics, leaderboard, friends): performance of the terms of use (GDPR article 6.1.b).
Securing the site (sessions, rate limiting, result checks): legitimate interest (GDPR article 6.1.f).
Sending the emails your account needs (forgotten password): performance of the terms of use.
No advertising, no audience measurement, no resale: your data is only used to run Calculus.

sections.title: What other players can see
body: Your username, Elo, leaderboard position, number of games, win rate, achievements, title and daily calc score are public. Achievements unlocked by an online game are shown to the players of that game.
Your profile photo is only visible to you, your friends and your guild members, who can also see whether you are online. A guild’s crest is visible to the signed-in players it invites.
Results of an online game (usernames, scores, answers) are visible to anyone with the link to its report, which is shared with the game’s players.
Your email address is never displayed. A player who already knows it can use it to send you a friend request.

sections.title: Our service providers
body: Your data is processed by technical providers, only to run the site:
Scalingo (hosting of the website, online games and database; French company, servers in France);
Resend (email delivery, United States);

voice input, if you turn it on: speech recognition is done by your browser, which may send the audio to its vendor (Google for Chrome, Apple for Safari, Microsoft for Edge). Calculus only receives the recognised number, never the audio.
Transfers to the United States are covered by the EU–US Data Privacy Framework or by the European Commission’s standard contractual clauses.

sections.title: How long we keep it
body: Account, games, statistics, friends and guild: as long as your account exists (the guild, until you leave it).
Sign-in sessions (IP address, browser): 30 days at most.
Password reset link: 1 hour. Game invitation: 10 minutes.
Feedback: while we handle it, then deleted at most one year later. It stays readable by the site team, unlinked from your account if you delete it.
When you delete your account, everything is erased: account, sessions, statistics, Elo, friends and solo games. Online games remain for the other players, but your username is removed from them.

sections.title: Cookies
body: Calculus only uses essential cookies: the one that keeps you signed in (30 days) and a session cache (5 minutes). No advertising or analytics cookies, which is why there is no banner to accept.

sections.title: Children
body: Calculus may be used by children, and we ask for as little data as possible. If you are under 15, ask a parent before creating an account. A parent can write to {contact} to have their child’s account deleted.

sections.title: Your rights
body: You can at any time access your data, correct it, have it erased, get a copy, object to or restrict its processing, and give instructions about what happens to it after your death.
Change your username: from your profile.
Delete your account: “Delete my account” button in your profile.
Any other request: write to {contact}. We reply within one month.
If you believe your rights are not respected, you can lodge a complaint with the CNIL, the French data protection authority (cnil.fr).

sections.title: Security

changelog.title: What’s new
changelog.noticeText: Calculus is now on version {version}: see what’s new.

v1_3_0: Dungeons: set off on an expedition with 2 to 4 players, by invitation or with a code, across a map of rooms on four floors, then face the boss together.
Dungeons: twelve enemies to defeat with your calculations, chests (beware of mimics), a two-item bag, lives, and the chance to revive a fallen ally.
Achievements: new dungeon achievements and two titles to unlock, “Adventurer” and “Scourge of the dungeons”.
Dashboard: your stats by difficulty (games, accuracy, average time, online wins, best streak), filterable by game.
On mobile, the site loads faster: fonts are now served directly by Calculus.
Fixes: the new-version banner no longer shows on your very first visit, and online, rejoining a game with the same account no longer removes you by mistake.
v1_2_0: Daily calc: five calculations from Easy to Legend, the same for everyone, one attempt a day and a daily leaderboard.
Achievements and titles: unlock achievements as you play and pick the title shown under your username from your profile.
Online: if your connection drops, the site reconnects you automatically and you get your place back in the game.
Lobby: the buttons to start or leave stay at the bottom of the screen while you set up the game.
On mobile, a game now starts at the top of the screen, with no header or footer.
Fixes: in solo on a phone, the correction is full width again, and “Next” no longer triggers by itself after tapping OK.
v1_1_0: Solo: after a mistake, the right answer stays on screen until you move on to the next one.
On mobile, the keypad stays docked at the bottom of the screen and each key reacts as soon as you press it.
Online speed race: a 4-second pause between rounds to see who scored and the right answer.
Games page: a “Play solo” button for each game, which picks up your last settings.
Home page: the warm-up has its own title, and on mobile the two main choices come first.
Text lines up better with the grid paper, and your light or dark theme now stays in place when you switch languages.
This what’s new page: the version number shows at the bottom of the page, and a banner announces each new version for 48 hours.
v1_0_0: Four games: mental math, right on target, missing number and the bomb.
Solo or up to twelve players online, in battle royale or speed race, across five levels.
Accounts with statistics, Elo and leaderboards per game, mode and level.
Friends, guilds, invites and public lobbies.
Mental math techniques to learn, practice drills and end-of-game tips.
Voice input, light or dark theme, in French and English.

learn.title: Mental math techniques
learn.intro: Tricks to calculate faster in your head, sorted by level. Each one comes with a worked example, step by step.

complement-10.name: Making 10
complement-10.summary: To add a small number, first fill up to the next ten, then add what is left.
complement-10.how: {a} + {c} = {ten} fills up the ten, then {rest} is left to add.

plus-minus-9.name: Adding or taking away 9
plus-minus-9.summary: 9 is 10 − 1: add (or take away) 10, then fix it by 1. It works with 19, 29… too.
plus-minus-9.how: {minus, plural, =1 {Take away {round} instead of {b}, then add 1 back.} other {Add {round} instead of {b}, then take 1 away.}}

near-doubles.name: Near doubles
near-doubles.summary: Two neighbouring numbers: start from the double you know, then add the gap.

complement-100.name: Making 100
complement-100.summary: For 100 minus a number, the tens go up to 9 and the units up to 10.
complement-100.how: Tens up to 9: {tens}; units up to 10: {units}. So {b} needs {complement} to make 100{hundreds, plural, =0 {.} other {, to add to the {hundreds} left over.}}

compensation-sub.name: Subtracting by compensation
compensation-sub.summary: Add the same number to both terms to land on a round ten: the difference stays the same.
compensation-sub.how: Add {c} to both numbers: {a} − {b} becomes {a2} − {b2}, much easier.

mul-by-11.name: Multiplying by 11
mul-by-11.summary: For a two-digit number, spread its digits apart and slip their sum in the middle.
mul-by-11.how: Spread {t} and {u} apart and slip their sum, {s}, in the middle{carry, plural, =1 {: it is over 9, so carry 1 to the hundreds.} other {.}}

distributivity.name: Splitting a factor
distributivity.summary: Split a factor into tens and units, multiply each part, then add them up.
distributivity.how: {x} = {tens} + {units}: work out {tens} × {y} and {units} × {y}, then add them.

mul-by-25.name: Multiplying by 25
mul-by-25.summary: 25 is 100 ÷ 4: multiply by 100, then divide by 4.

square-ending-5.name: Squaring a number ending in 5
square-ending-5.summary: Multiply the tens digit by the next number, then write 25 at the end.

div-by-steps.name: Dividing in two steps
div-by-steps.summary: A divisor that splits up (6 = 2 × 3) can be done as two easy divisions. Divisibility rules (even, sum of digits…) tell you where to start.

regroup-factors.name: Regrouping factors
regroup-factors.summary: In a chain of multiplications the order does not matter: bring together the ones that make a round number.

diff-squares.name: Around a round number
diff-squares.summary: Two numbers the same distance from a round number: (m − d) × (m + d) = m² − d².
diff-squares.how: {x} and {y} are {d} away from {m}: work out {m}² − {d}².

div-by-25.name: Dividing by 25
div-by-25.summary: There are four 25s in 100: multiply by 4, then divide by 100.

neighbor-square.name: Squaring a neighbour
neighbor-square.summary: For a number right next to a ten: (m ± 1)² = m² ± 2m + 1.
neighbor-square.how: {n} is just {below, plural, =1 {before} other {after}} {m}: {m}² = {square}, then {below, plural, =1 {take away} other {add}} 2 × {m} {below, plural, =1 {−} other {+}} 1 = {gap}.

powers-of-2.name: Powers of 2
powers-of-2.summary: Remember two landmarks, 2⁵ = 32 and 2¹⁰ = 1024, then double or halve.
powers-of-2.how: Start from the landmark 2 to the power {ref} = {refValue}, then {down, plural, =1 {halve} other {double}} {count, plural, one {once} =2 {twice} other {# times}}.

sqrt-bracketing.name: Square roots by bracketing
sqrt-bracketing.summary: Squeeze the number between the squares of two tens, then look at its last digit.
sqrt-bracketing.how: {n} is between {low}² and {high}², so its root is between {low} and {high}. {single, plural, =1 {It ends in 5: it is {root}.} other {It ends in {last}: {cand1} or {cand2}. {mid}² decides: it is {root}.}}

mul-by-15.name: Multiplying by 15
mul-by-15.how: Work out {n} × 10, then add half of it.

daily.title: Daily calc
daily.cardSub: {rounds} calculations from Easy to Legend, the same for everyone. One attempt.
daily.lede: {rounds} calculations, from Easy to Legend, the same for every player today. You only get one attempt. Correct answers count first, then total time.
daily.rule: Only answering time counts, not corrections.
daily.guestNote: No account needed to play: you can log in or sign up at the end to save your score.
daily.error: The server isn’t responding. Your attempt isn’t lost: reload the page to resume it.
daily.wouldRank: With an account, you’d be #{rank} today.
daily.saveText: Log in or sign up now to enter today’s leaderboard.
daily.boardRule: The best score at midnight wins the “Daily champion” achievement.
daily.boardEmpty: Nobody is ranked for this day yet.

dungeon.title: Dungeons

rules.rounds: A map of rooms over four floors: each round, everyone picks an open room. A cleared room opens the ones beyond it.
rules.positioning: You must open the boss room before the end of round 4, or the expedition is lost. Several of you in the same room means several chances.
rules.perfect: An enemy is a series of calculations to get entirely right (except the hydra and the horde, which have their own rules).
rules.lives: Three lives each. Chests and fearsome enemies drop loot: hearts, shields, keys, bombs…
rules.boss: Broken seals weaken the boss, which the whole team fights together in round 5, against the clock.

dungeon.createText: You pick the difficulty, then invite your friends or give them the code.
dungeon.notEnough: You need at least {count} players to enter the dungeon.
dungeon.hostHint: You’re the host: pick the difficulty, then enter when the team is ready.
dungeon.inspectHint: Hover or tap a room to see what it holds.
dungeon.pickHint: Tap a lit room to go there: it’s reachable from a cleared room.
dungeon.lockHint: You can still change your mind, or lock your choice.
dungeon.locked: Choice locked. Waiting for the rest of the team.
dungeon.downWatching: You’re down: you’re watching your team. A heart will get you back up.
dungeon.mummyHint: The mummy hid the calculation: answer from memory.
dungeon.lootHint: If you don’t choose, you keep it (or it goes to the ally who needs it most if you have no room).
dungeon.lootPending: {name} is choosing who gets their heart…
dungeon.lootLost: {item} was lost: nobody had room left.

boss.name: The boss
boss.damage: {count, plural, =0 {no hits} one {# hit} other {# hits}}
boss.desc: It waits at the top of the dungeon. The whole team fights it together, against the clock: each correct answer takes a HP, each mistake costs a life. Seals broken on the way weaken it.

reason.no-enemy-defeated: No enemy was defeated during a round.
reason.boss-timeout: The boss held out until time ran out.
reason.boss-not-reached: The boss room wasn’t reached in time.

end.hostHint: Play again brings the whole team back to the waiting room.
end.waitHost: Waiting for the host to start a new expedition.

elf.name: Elf
elf.desc: Very simple calculations, but hardly any time for each.

troll.name: Troll
troll.desc: Big simple calculations: three-digit additions and subtractions, with time to work them out.

knight.name: Knight
knight.desc: A balanced opponent: calculations at the game’s level, with the usual time.

mummy.name: Mummy
mummy.desc: The calculation shows for one second only: remember it to answer.

witch.name: Witch
witch.desc: She hides a number in the equation: find what’s missing.

specter.name: Specter
specter.desc: It makes the operator vanish: plus, minus, times or divided? Answer with the right sign.

cyclops.name: Cyclops
cyclops.desc: A single, huge calculation, with plenty of time. All or nothing.

skeleton.name: Skeleton archer
skeleton.desc: Simple calculations, but every arrow flies faster than the last.

hydra.name: Hydra
hydra.desc: A mistake doesn’t fail you: two heads grow back (two more calculations). Finish before the clock runs out.

goblins.name: Goblin horde
goblins.desc: Lots of small calculations, shared by everyone fighting it: each correct answer takes down a goblin.

dragon.name: Dragon
dragon.desc: Powers and roots. It guards a shortcut: defeating it opens the boss room directly.

mimic.name: Mimic
mimic.desc: A chest… that bites. Defeated, it drops a rare item.

heart.name: Heart
heart.desc: One more life, for you or an ally (who gets back up if down).

shield.name: Shield
shield.desc: Your next failure costs no life. Works on its own.

hourglass.name: Hourglass
hourglass.desc: 50% more time on your next series.

second-chance.name: Second chance
second-chance.desc: Your first mistake in your next series is forgiven.

key.name: Key
key.desc: Pass an open room without fighting (no points, loot or seal).

bomb.name: Bomb
bomb.desc: Against the boss: takes 3 hit points at once.

phoenix.name: Phoenix feather
phoenix.desc: If you drop to 0 lives, you get back up with 1. Works on its own.

banner.name: Banner
banner.desc: One more life for the whole team.

purse.name: Gold purse
purse.desc: 250 points at the end of the expedition, while it’s in a bag.

map.name: Map
map.desc: Lifts the fog over the whole dungeon (mimics stay disguised).

kinds.unknownDesc: Still hidden in the fog. Move forward to find out what’s inside.
kinds.enemyDesc: An enemy awaits here; get closer to see which one.
kinds.sealDesc: Breaking this seal weakens the boss (−20% hit points).
kinds.sealShadowDesc: A seal guarded by an enemy: breaking it weakens the boss.
kinds.chestDesc: A loot item, no fight. Going there takes your round… and some chests bite.

dungeon.sealsHint: Each broken seal takes 20% of the boss’s hit points.
dungeon.keyMode: Tap the open room to unlock with the key.
dungeon.chestTaken: You took the chest: your loot awaits at the end of the round.
dungeon.cardHydra: {count} heads to start, {time} to cut them all
dungeon.roundCleared: {count, plural, =0 {No room cleared} one {# room cleared} other {# rooms cleared}} · +{points} points
dungeon.sealsBrokenNews: {count, plural, one {A seal broke: the boss weakens.} other {# seals broke: the boss weakens.}}
dungeon.bossWeakened: {count, plural, one {Weakened by # broken seal} other {Weakened by # broken seals}}

book.title: The monster book
book.intro: What awaits you in the corridors. The stars tell how strong each enemy is.

banned.title: Account suspended
banned.text: This account is suspended: the daily challenge, online lobbies and dungeons are closed to it. Solo play stays open.
banned.appeal: Think this is a mistake? Write to us and a person will review your case.
